docs.title: Massage Salon — Saanenland
docs.text:
We are opening a massage salon in the Saanenland region (Gstaad / Saanen, Canton of Bern). These pages hold the full plan: business setup, website, legal requirements, online visibility, marketing, and online booking.

Читать на русском → (or use the 文A icon at the top).

docs.title: Goals
docs.text:
1. A professional website for the salon.
  2. Compliant with Swiss law (company, website, ads, privacy).
  3. A .ch domain.
  4. Marketing: Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, Google, AI assistants (ChatGPT etc.); maybe TikTok/YouTube; other relevant channels.
  5. Shown in Google and other search engines/maps with address, contacts, working hours.

docs.title: Business setup & verifications (Switzerland, Canton of Bern)
docs.text:
Research notes, not legal advice. Items marked [verify] must be confirmed with the named authority or a Swiss fiduciary (Treuhänder) before acting.

The order matters: almost every online verification (Google, Meta, WhatsApp, ad accounts) asks for proof that the business exists at a real address. So the legal/physical setup comes first.

docs.title: A1. Choose legal form
docs.text:
Form Commercial register Liability Notes Sole proprietorship (Einzelunternehmen) Required once turnover ≥ CHF 100,000/yr; voluntary below Personal, unlimited Cheapest, fastest. Owner must have Swiss residence/work permit allowing self-employment [verify] GmbH Always required Limited to company Min. capital CHF 20,000, notary deed. Better with several partners Partnership (Kollektivgesellschaft) Required Partners personally For 2+ partners without a GmbH

With several partners, a GmbH is usually the cleaner choice (clear shares, limited liability). Decide with a fiduciary.

docs.title: A2. Name check & registration
docs.text:
• Check name availability: zefix.ch (central business name index) plus trademarks at swissreg.ch.
  • Register with the Handelsregisteramt des Kantons Bern. Online via EasyGov.swiss, which also handles AHV, VAT and accident insurance in one go.
  • You receive a UID number (CHE-xxx.xxx.xxx). It goes in the Impressum and is used for platform verifications.

docs.title: A3. Social insurance & tax
docs.text:
• AHV/AVS (self-employed status): register with the Ausgleichskasse des Kantons Bern. They decide whether you count as self-employed. Platforms and banks may ask for this.
  • Employees: AHV contributions, mandatory accident insurance (UVG), and BVG (pension) above the threshold.
  • VAT (MWST): mandatory from CHF 100,000 annual turnover. Below that it's optional. Note: some medical treatments are VAT-exempt, but wellness massage is not [verify].

docs.title: A4. Professional permits (depends on the services offered)
docs.text:
• Wellness / classic massage (no medical claims): generally no cantonal health licence in Canton of Bern [verify with GSI Bern].
  • Medical massage (Medizinische/r Masseur/in with eidg. Fachausweis, treatment on prescription): needs a cantonal professional practice licence (Berufsausübungsbewilligung) from the Gesundheits-, Sozial- und Integrationsdirektion (GSI) of Canton Bern [verify].
  • Insurance reimbursement (a big selling point in CH): therapists register with ASCA and/or EMR. Customers' supplementary insurance then covers part of the cost. Requirements include a recognised qualification, continuing education, and liability insurance. The registration is per therapist, not per salon.
  • Foreign qualifications may need recognition by the SRK (Swiss Red Cross) for medical massage [verify].
  • Work permits: any non-Swiss partners or staff need a permit that allows (self-)employment.

docs.title: A5. Premises (Gemeinde Saanen / Gsteig / Lauenen)
docs.text:
• Check that the zoning allows commercial use. Converting a flat or chalet room may need a change-of-use permit (Nutzungsänderung / Baubewilligung) from the municipality [verify].
  • Rental contract in the business name. It's the address proof for every platform.
  • Visible signage at the door. Google Business Profile verification often requires it (video verification).
  • Hygiene and fire-safety basics. Contact the municipality building office (Bauverwaltung Saanen).

docs.title: A6. Insurance
docs.text:
• Professional liability (Berufshaftpflicht). Required for ASCA/EMR, and essential in any case.
  • Business contents/property insurance and loss-of-earnings (daily allowance) insurance.

docs.title: A7. Bank & payments
docs.text:
• Business bank account (needs the commercial register extract or UID plus ID).
  • Card terminal and TWINT (expected in Switzerland). Online payment provider later for deposits/no-show fees.

docs.title: C. Suggested order
docs.text:
1. Name shortlist → Zefix + domain + social handles availability (same day, so nobody grabs them)
  2. Legal form decision with fiduciary → registration (EasyGov) → UID
  3. Premises contract + municipality check + signage
  4. Bank, insurance, AHV, permits (if medical), ASCA/EMR applications
  5. Register the domain → business email on the domain (needed for Meta/Google verifications)
  6. Google Business Profile, Meta Business, WhatsApp, Apple, Bing, local.ch
  7. Website live → link everything together

docs.title: Website & marketing law (Switzerland)
docs.text: Research notes, not legal advice. [verify] = confirm before launch.

docs.title: To research
docs.text:
• Impressum: required by UWG Art. 3 para. 1 lit. s for online offers. It must show the legal name, address, contact email and UID.
  • Privacy policy under revFADP (nDSG, in force since 2023-09-01). It must list:
  • the data collected (contact form, booking, analytics, pixels)
  • processors and countries
  • customers' rights
  • Health data: booking notes about health conditions are sensitive personal data. Minimise what's collected, store it securely, and state this in the privacy policy.
  • Cookies/tracking: Swiss law is lighter than the EU's, but EU visitors and Meta/Google pixels make a consent banner sensible [verify].
  • Advertising:
  • No misleading health or healing claims. Wellness massage must not promise to cure anything.
  • The therapeutic-products and health law limits medical advertising [verify].
  • Prices: the Price Indication Ordinance (PBV) requires clear final prices in CHF, including VAT if VAT-registered [verify].
  • Accessibility: good practice (WCAG), not strictly mandatory for private businesses.
  • Terms: cancellation and no-show policy for bookings, payment and deposit rules. Not needed at launch: cash only, no fees or deposits (decision 2026-10-24). Revisit with card payments, prepaid packages or online vouchers.

docs.text: • Prefer Switzerland or the EU, which simplifies the privacy policy. Depends on the stack (undecided).

  • Set up SPF/DKIM/DMARC from day one, so booking confirmations don't land in spam.

docs.text:
• Technical plan for ads, SEO and analytics: Website: ads, SEO and analytics.

docs.title: Local search presence
docs.text: Goal: appear with address, phone, hours, photos and reviews when someone searches "massage Gstaad" on Google, Apple Maps, Bing, or asks an AI assistant.

docs.title: Channels
docs.text:
• Google Business Profile. Most important. Fill in:
  • categories, services, hours, holiday hours, photos, booking link
  • answers to Q&A, and replies to every review
  • Bing Places. Feeds ChatGPT and Copilot search.
  • Apple Business Connect. Feeds Apple Maps and Siri. Many tourists use iPhones.
  • local.ch / search.ch. Swiss directories.
  • Gstaad Saanenland Tourismus listing, plus hotel and chalet-agency guest guides.
  • TripAdvisor (tourists), possibly booking platforms.

docs.title: Booking link in listings
docs.text:
• The booking tool does not do local SEO for us. All the listings above are our own work.
  • Google Business Profile: add the booking link as the "Appointment URL". Google's built-in booking button ("Reserve with Google") works only with partner tools. Fresha is one; Cal.com most likely is not [verify].
  • See Booking tool: buy or build?.

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
• Name, address and phone exactly as in business.yml, everywhere.
  • Ask happy clients for reviews in their language. Never buy or gate reviews.
  • Website: schema.org markup, a page per treatment and language, an embedded map.

docs.title: Marketing
docs.text:
The booking tool does not bring clients

A booking tool (e.g. Cal.com) only handles scheduling: calendar, free slots, booking form, confirmations, reminders. Finding clients is our own work, whichever tool we choose: our .ch website and its SEO, Google Business Profile and other listings, ads, social media, reviews and partnerships. Only marketplace tools such as Fresha add some visibility of their own, for a 20% fee on new marketplace clients. Details: Booking tool: buy or build?.

docs.title: Where ads and links point
docs.text:
• All ads (Google, Meta) land on our website, on the page for the right treatment and language, not directly on the booking tool. The website carries the SEO value, the ad tracking and the trust (photos, prices, reviews).
  • The website has a "Book" button in every language. It opens the booking tool, e.g. as a popup. The button text must be translated per language: "Termin buchen" / "Book now" / "Réserver" / "Prenota".
  • Google Business Profile, Instagram and Facebook: the booking link is added as the "Appointment URL", in the bio and on the "Book now" button.
  • A booking page on the tool's domain (e.g. cal.com/...) does not improve our search ranking. SEO comes only from our own domain.

docs.title: Regional targeting (Saanenland)
docs.text:
• Small resident population. Most demand comes from visitors.
  • Ad targeting:
  • Meta: a radius around Gstaad, with "people living in or recently in / travelling to" the area.
  • Google: start with "presence" (people in or regularly in the area); test "presence or interest" (also people planning a trip) before the winter season. Plus search terms like "massage Gstaad" in every language. See Ads.
  • Watch for audiences that are too small for Meta. You may need a wider radius (e.g. include Zweisimmen, Château-d'Œx) or interest/lookalike layers.
  • Seasonality:
  • Peaks: winter (Dec–Mar) and summer (Jul–Aug).
  • Events: Menuhin Festival, Swiss Open tennis, polo, Hublot Polo Gold Cup, etc. [check calendar]
  • Tourist peaks: winter (Dec–Mar) and summer (Jul–Aug). Raise tourist-targeted ads then.
  • Anti-cellulite demand peaks in spring (Mar–Jun), before summer. That is low tourist season, so in Apr–Jun target locals and second-home owners instead of pausing.
  • Pause or cut ads in November.

docs.title: Self-managed advertising plan
docs.text: We run marketing ourselves, with no agency (see the comparison below). Most bookings are expected from free channels; paid ads come on top. Concrete budgets and cost limits are in the private notes (private/marketing-budget.md).

docs.title: 1. Free channels first
docs.text: Channel What to do Google Business Profile Most important. Category "Massage", photos, hours, prices, booking link as "Appointment URL", regular posts. Ask every happy client for a review, in their language (see Local search presence) Apple Business Connect, Bing Places, local.ch / search.ch Same name, address and phone everywhere. Bing feeds ChatGPT/Copilot answers; Apple feeds iPhone Maps (many tourists) Instagram (organic) 2–3 short Reels a week: the studio, hands and oil, the village, "free slot tomorrow at 10:00". Booking link in the bio WhatsApp Business Quick replies, a catalog with the treatment and packages, a status update when slots free up Local partners Likely the strongest channel. Hotels, chalet agencies and concierges: cards with a QR code, plus a commission or a free session. Gyms, yoga studios, hairdressers, nail studios: swap referrals. Gstaad Saanenland Tourismus listing Local print An ad or short article in the local paper (Anzeiger von Saanen) at opening [verify]. Flyers at Saanen station and in local shops

docs.title: 2. Paid ads we run ourselves
docs.text:
Step-by-step setup, content requirements and languages: Ads.

  • Google Search Ads (start here).
  • Keywords in DE/EN/FR/IT, e.g. "Anti-Cellulite Massage Saanen", "Massage Gstaad", "Cellulite Massage Gstaad".
  • Location: start with people in Saanenland ("presence"); before the winter season, test adding people interested in it, so tourists planning a trip also see the ads.
  • Ads lead to our website, in the matching language, not to the booking tool.
  • Search volume in Saanenland is small: start with a small daily test budget.
  • Meta (Instagram + Facebook).
  • Area: about 15–25 km around Saanen, "people living in or recently in this area".
  • 2–3 ad creatives: the studio, the treatment mood, the trial-session offer.
  • Ads lead to our website or open a WhatsApp chat.
  • Test, then keep what works. Run each campaign 4–6 weeks, then keep only what brings bookings below our cost limit.

Ad rules for anti-cellulite

  • No before/after photos. Meta bans them for cosmetic and weight-related ads.
  • No negative body image, e.g. "Hate your cellulite?"
  • No medical promises such as "removes cellulite", "detox" or "minus one size". Use wording like "smoother, firmer-looking skin" and note that results vary.
  • Massage is a restricted category on Meta and Google: wellness imagery only.

docs.title: 3. Tracking
docs.text:
Technical details: Website: ads, SEO and analytics.

  • Add UTM tags to every link (e.g. ?utm_source=instagram&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=spring-2027) to see which channel brings bookings. Allowed values and all links: UTM links.
  • The Meta pixel and Google Ads conversion tracking need a cookie consent banner on the website (see Website & marketing law).
  • Main number: cost per booking. A client who buys a package is worth much more than one visit, so a higher cost for a first booking can still pay off.

docs.title: 4. Doing it ourselves vs. paying someone
docs.text:
Option How you pay Worth it for us? Ourselves (Google Ads + Meta Ads Manager) Only the ad spend, plus about 2–4 hours a week ✅ Yes: cheapest at our size Agency / freelancer managing ads Monthly fee or a share of ad spend, often with a minimum ❌ No: with a small budget the fee can be higher than the ads themselves Freelancer for one-off setup One-off fee (accounts, first campaigns, tracking) ⚠️ Maybe, if nobody wants to learn the ad tools Booking marketplace (Fresha; Treatwell also operates in Switzerland [verify]) Commission only per new client (Fresha: 20% of the first booking) ✅ Worth trying: pay per result, no upfront risk. There may be few marketplace users in Saanen Discount deal sites (Groupon-style) Big discount plus commission ❌ No: attracts one-time bargain hunters, not package clients

Agency fees and real cost per click vary a lot. Treat this as an estimate; get one or two quotes if needed. Only a 4–6 week test shows our real cost per booking.

docs.title: 5. Rollout
docs.text:
1. Before opening: all free channels from section 1; first reviews from real visits by friends and family.
  2. First 1–2 months: Google Search ads run by us; Meta from March; the Fresha marketplace if we choose Fresha.
  3. After 6–8 weeks: keep only channels with a cost per booking below our limit.

docs.title: KPIs (to define)
docs.text: Bookings per channel, cost per booking, review count/rating, repeat clients.

docs.title: Goal
docs.text: A client can book from the website, Instagram, WhatsApp, Google Maps, and AI chats (ChatGPT etc.). All channels write to one calendar, so there are no double bookings.

docs.title: Options to evaluate
docs.text:
1. SaaS booking platform with integrations (e.g. SimplyBook.me, Fresha, Setmore, Square Appointments) [compare].
  2. Launch comparison and buy-vs-build estimate: Booking tool: buy or build?.
  3. Often already connects to Reserve with Google and the Instagram/Facebook "Book" button.
  4. Check that it has an API, supports DE/EN/FR/IT, CHF, TWINT, and has Swiss/EU data hosting.
  5. Custom backend (fits if the site is Rails): own API, with SaaS-like channel integrations built step by step.

docs.title: AI chat channel
docs.text:
• WhatsApp: needs the WhatsApp Business API (Meta verification, see 01-business-setup-ch.md). An AI agent answers in the client's language and books via the backend API.
  • ChatGPT / Claude / other assistants: expose availability and booking as a tool (e.g. an MCP server or app). This needs a backend with a clean API, which favours option 2 or a SaaS with a good API.
  • Rules: confirm before booking, collect the minimum personal data, no health advice, hand over to a human easily.

docs.title: Phase-1 decisions that must not block this
docs.text:
• Choose a stack and booking tool that have an API.
  • Use one phone number for WhatsApp that can later move to the API.
  • Keep services, durations and prices in business.yml with stable IDs.

docs.title: Booking tool: buy or build?
docs.text: Researched 2026-10-16. Prices change often: check each vendor's site before signing up.

docs.title: Situation
docs.text:
• At launch the salon has one master, who is also a partner.
  • The salon offers beauty / wellness only, with no medical massage. Health-insurance tools (ASCA/EMR receipts, OneDoc) are not needed.
  • The owner is a backend developer and could build a custom booking system.

Decision 2026-10-24: Cal.com (see Decisions). Dikidi was tested in the prototype and dropped. The research below is kept for reference.

docs.title: Recommendation
docs.text:
Use a ready-made booking tool at launch. Build only the salon website, and embed the tool's "Book now" widget in it. Review the choice after 6–12 months, or once there are 3 or more masters.

After the language check below, only Fresha and Cal.com remain: they are the only ones whose booking pages cover DE, EN, FR and IT. Fresha is the main candidate, because it also brings some new clients. Cal.com is the backup if we want more control.

docs.title: Ready-made tools (one master)
docs.text:
Tool Approx. price Good Less good Fresha (Independent plan) ~USD 19.95/month (~CHF 16), ~CHF 190/year. A cheaper EU price list (~EUR 12.95) is also reported [verify]. Card fees, plus a 20% fee on new clients who come through the Fresha marketplace Polished, multilingual, Reserve with Google, marketplace brings new clients Marketplace fee on new clients Dikidi Core features free. Paid add-ons are optional, and prices are shown only in the app [verify] Cheapest, simple, good mobile apps. Known among Ukrainian/Russian-speaking clients No German, French or Italian (see language check). Little known among Swiss clients Cal.com Free for one person. Open source, so it can be self-hosted later Developer-friendly, has an API, easy path to a custom system later Generic scheduling tool, not salon-specific (no vouchers, stock, etc.) SimplyBook.me Free tier with limits; paid plans above that [verify] Many add-ons (vouchers, payments) Interface feels dated Altegio (international version of YCLIENTS) Smallest plan is for 2 employees, at a much higher price Very feature-rich, scales to chains No German (see language check). Too much and too expensive for one master

Before choosing, check each tool for: - DE / EN / FR / IT booking pages - CHF prices, and TWINT or card payments - Reserve with Google, plus the Instagram and Facebook "Book" buttons - Gift vouchers (useful for tourists in Gstaad) - A data processing agreement and data hosting compatible with the Swiss data protection law (revFADP / nDSG) - An API, needed for Phase 2 (see Phase 2: Booking everywhere)

docs.title: Language check (DE / EN / FR / IT)
docs.text:
Checked 2026-10-16. The booking page must be fully available in our four website languages.

Tool DE EN FR IT How it was checked Fresha ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ The client app lists all four (App Store, Switzerland). fresha.com has real DE/FR/IT pages Cal.com ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ Open-source code has DE/FR/IT translations (~97% of the English text). The page follows the visitor's browser language SimplyBook.me ⚠️ ✅ ⚠️ ⚠️ One booking-page language at a time. Several languages only through an automatic Google Translate add-on (machine translation) Dikidi ❌ ✅ ❌ ❌ App only in EN, KK (Kazakh), PT, RU; website only in EN, KK, RU Altegio ❌ ✅ ✅ ✅ Official list of 23 widget languages (updated 2026-09-01) has no German

German is the local language in Gstaad (Canton of Bern), so Dikidi and Altegio are ruled out.

Our own texts

The tools translate their own interface (buttons, calendar, emails). Texts we write ourselves (service names, descriptions, cancellation rules) are usually stored in one language only. During the trial, check:

  1. Can each service name and description be entered in all four languages?
  2. Are confirmations and reminders sent in the client's language?

If not, use short bilingual service names, e.g. "Klassische Massage / Classic massage 60 min".

docs.title: Cal.com test (2026-10-16)
docs.text:
• The floating "Book" button embed works on a plain test page: a button in the corner opens the calendar in a popup.
  • The popup can show or hide the service details (name, duration, description) next to the calendar.
  • The button text is fixed in the embed code (default: "Book my Cal"). It does not change with the visitor's language. On our multilingual site, each language version must set its own text, e.g. "Termin buchen" / "Book now" / "Réserver" / "Prenota".

docs.title: Booking tool vs. finding clients
docs.text:
A booking tool such as Cal.com only handles scheduling: the calendar, free slots, the booking form, confirmations and reminders. It does not bring clients. Everything that makes people find us stays our work, whichever tool we choose:

  • SEO: our own .ch website in DE/EN/FR/IT (see Website). A booking page on cal.com does not help our search ranking, because it is not on our domain.
  • Google Business Profile: add the booking link as the "Appointment URL" (see Local search presence). As far as we know, Cal.com is not a "Reserve with Google" partner [verify], so clients click through to our link instead of booking inside Google.
  • Instagram / Facebook: booking link in the bio and on the "Book now" button.
  • Ads (Google, Meta): point to our website, not to the booking tool (see Marketing).
  • Reviews, local directories (local.ch, search.ch), hotel/concierge partnerships.

Difference with Fresha: Fresha also helps with finding clients, through its marketplace (people searching for a massage nearby) and Reserve with Google. The price is a 20% fee on new marketplace clients.

  • Cal.com: free and full control, but all new clients come from our own site and marketing.
  • Fresha: small subscription plus a fee on new marketplace clients, but some extra visibility from day one.

docs.title: Building our own system
docs.text:
What a minimal version needs: services with durations and prices, the master's working hours, free-slot calculation, a booking form, email confirmations and reminders, cancel/reschedule links, a simple admin page, and calendar sync.

Item Estimate Development 60–120 hours Hosting (small server + database) CHF 5–15/month SMS reminders (optional) ~CHF 0.07–0.10 per SMS Email delivery Usually free at this volume Online payments (TWINT/card) Same transaction fees as with a ready-made tool Ongoing support: updates, security, backups, bugs 2–5 hours/month Data protection The salon alone is responsible for storing client data safely

What we would not get from a self-built system on day one: - New clients from the platform: marketplace listings (Fresha, Dikidi catalog). A custom system only gets visitors through our own website and SEO. - Booking from other apps: Reserve with Google and the Instagram/Facebook "Book" buttons need partner approval or extra integration work. - A mobile app for the master with notifications for new bookings. - Extra features: gift vouchers, reviews, deposits and no-show protection.

docs.title: Conclusion
docs.text:
With one master, a ready-made tool costs about CHF 0–200 per year. Building our own costs months of the owner's time, plus ongoing maintenance, and it would take many years to pay back.

Building our own makes sense only if one of these becomes true: - There are 3 or more masters or several locations, so per-person subscriptions grow. - We have needs no tool covers (for example, hotel/chalet partnerships with home visits, or unusual packages). - We decide to make a booking product for other salons. That would be a separate business.

A good middle step is Cal.com: free now, and it can later be self-hosted behind our own website.

docs.title: Meeting: questions before we start
docs.text:
Prepared 2026-10-19. One list of everything we need to decide before building the real website and opening the salon.

How to use this page in the meeting

  • Go through the sections in order. Section A blocks everything else, so do it first.
  • For each question, write down the answer, who takes it on, and by when.
  • After the meeting, answers move into Decisions, Business facts or the topic pages, and the question is removed here.
  • Sensitive answers (partner shares, money, budgets, personal data) are not written on this public site. They go into the private notes (private/).

docs.title: A. Business & legal (blocking)
docs.text:
• 1. Salon name. What is the final name?
    • Why: needed for the commercial register, the .ch domain, Instagram/Facebook handles and the logo.
    • Next step: check availability in Zefix, for the .ch domain and for the social handles.
  • 2. Partners and roles. Who are the partners, and who does what?
    • Roles to cover: therapist, website & tech, marketing & social media, admin & bookkeeping, client communication.
    • Shares and money: private notes only.
  • 3. Legal form. Sole proprietorship (Einzelunternehmen), partnership (Kollektivgesellschaft) or GmbH?
    • Depends on question 2 and on liability. See Business setup.
  • 4. Therapist. Qualifications and diplomas, recognition of a foreign diploma if needed, and a work/residence permit that allows this work.
  • 5. Fiduciary (Treuhänder). Do we use one for registration, bookkeeping and a legal check of the website before launch? Who?
  • 6. Bank and payments. Business bank account, TWINT for business, card terminal (e.g. SumUp) or not?
  • 7. Insurance. Professional liability (Berufshaftpflicht), contents/premises insurance, accident insurance.
  • 8. VAT (MWST). Do we expect less than CHF 100,000 turnover a year (no VAT needed), or do we register voluntarily?

docs.title: B. Premises
docs.text:
• 9. Address. What is the real address? Dorfstrasse 1, 3792 Saanen in the prototype is only a sample.
  • 10. Use of the premises. Is commercial use allowed? Do we need a change-of-use permit? Can we put up a sign?
  • 11. Parking. Which car parks do we recommend to clients? Are there private spaces? Fees and payment methods [verify] on site.
  • 12. Opening date. Target date, and what must be ready by then (equipment, linen, oils, furniture)?

docs.title: C. Service, prices and rules
docs.text:
• 13. Services at launch. Only the anti-cellulite massage? Which services may come later?
  • 14. Durations. Trial session 45 min and regular session 60 min, or different?
  • 15. Prices. Final prices for the trial session, a single session and the packages.
    • Note: the prototype shows CHF 130 for 60 min, but the Dikidi account shows CHF 100. One price everywhere.
  • 16. Packages. 5 and 10 sessions? How long are they valid? Paid in advance?
  • 17. Cancellation and no-shows. ✅ Decided 2026-10-24: no cancellation or no-show fees, no deposit (cash only). Clients are asked to cancel as early as possible.
  • 18. Opening hours. Days and hours, seasonal changes, holidays and closures.
  • 19. Languages. Which languages does the therapist speak with clients?
  • 20. Gift vouchers. At launch or later? Sold online, in the studio, or both?
  • 21. Payment in the studio. ✅ Decided 2026-10-24: cash only at launch, no online prepayment.
  • 22. Client health questions. Do we ask about contraindications (pregnancy, varicose veins, recent surgery…) before the first session?
    • Why: health data is sensitive personal data under Swiss data protection law. If we collect it, we need a clear process: paper or digital, where it is stored, who can see it.

docs.title: D. Booking tool
docs.text:
• 23. Which tool? ✅ Decided 2026-10-24: Cal.com. See Booking tool: buy or build?.
    • Open: the booking screen follows the visitor's browser language. Do we want one Cal.com event type per language, so it always matches the page? See Booking calendar language.
    • Criteria: booking screens in DE/EN/FR/IT, a "Book" button inside Instagram/Facebook, booking from Google Maps, cost, ease of use for the therapist.
    • Test result so far: Cal.com follows the visitor's language. Dikidi opened in English, showed one Russian label ("Без категории", "No category") and its own cookie banner.
  • 24. Account owner. In whose name is the account, and which email and phone are used?
  • 25. Reminders. Email only, or also SMS/WhatsApp reminders (may cost extra)?
  • 26. Data we ask for at booking. Minimum: name, phone, email? Anything else?
  • 27. Public profile. What may be shown in the booking window: the therapist's name, photo, location?

docs.title: E. Website
docs.text:
• 28. Technology. Simple static site (like the prototype), Rails, or a site builder? Who maintains it?
  • 29. Domain. Which .ch domain? Also .swiss and common misspellings? Registered in the company's name, with which registrar? Who holds the login?
  • 30. Email. Business addresses on the domain (e.g. info@, booking@)? Which provider?
  • 31. Design. Keep the prototype's style and colours? Who designs the logo?
  • 32. Photos. Professional photoshoot of the studio and the treatment? (No before/after photos; see the ad rules in Marketing.)
  • 33. Texts and translations. Who writes the texts, and who approves them? Who translates into DE/FR/IT (native speakers, not machine translation, especially for the legal pages)?
  • 34. More languages later. e.g. RU, UK, AR, ZH: which ones, and when?
  • 35. Legal pages. Impressum data, privacy policy and cookie banner. Who checks them before launch (fiduciary or lawyer)?

docs.title: F. Marketing
docs.text:
• 36. Social accounts. Which do we create (Instagram, Facebook, TikTok, YouTube, WhatsApp Business), with which handles? Who posts, and how often?
  • 37. Google Business Profile. Who owns and manages it? Verification needs the real address (by postcard or video).
  • 38. WhatsApp number. Which phone number is the business number? It should be able to move to the WhatsApp Business API later.
  • 39. Ad budget. Monthly budget per season (private notes only). See the plan in Marketing.
  • 40. Who runs the ads? Ourselves (recommended) or a freelancer for the first setup? How many hours per week?
  • 41. Local partners. Which hotels, chalet agencies, gyms and salons do we contact? Who contacts them? What do we offer (commission, free session, cards with a QR code)?
  • 42. Opening offer. A special trial-session price or an opening event?
  • 43. Reviews. How do we ask clients for Google reviews (a card with a QR code, a message after the visit)?

docs.title: G. Later (Phase 2)
docs.text:
• 44. Booking from WhatsApp and AI assistants. When do we start? See Phase 2: Booking everywhere.
  • 45. A second therapist. At what point (bookings per week, waiting list) do we hire?

docs.text:
Research from 2026-10-21. Prices and menus change often: check them on each provider's site before you sign up.

A step-by-step guide for opening the salon's online accounts before the salon opens.

docs.title: Situation
docs.text:
• Salon name: not decided yet. It blocks almost everything, because Google, Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp all show it.
  • Login email: the therapist has a separate Gmail address for the business. This is fine.
  • Business phone: none yet. The plan for now is to use the therapist's private number (see Phone number).
  • Premises: the contract is signed. The keys come in December 2026.
  • Goal: have everything set up before December, and ideally have first clients booked for the opening.

docs.title: Order of steps
docs.text:
1. Decide the salon name. Check it in Zefix, check the .ch domain and the social media handles.
  2. Get a second phone number on an eSIM (recommended, see below).
  3. Create the Facebook Page, then the Business Portfolio (add a second admin), then the Instagram professional account linked to the Page.
  4. Install WhatsApp Business on the salon number and link it to the Page and Instagram.
  5. Create the Google Business Profile now, choose "Verify later", and set the opening date.
  6. Buy the domain and set up the email (info@salonname.ch).
  7. December: put up a sign (a temporary one is fine), then verify Google by video.

docs.title: Login email and access
docs.text:
A separate Gmail address is fine as the login for Google, Meta, the booking tool and other platforms. Google Business Profile needs a Google account anyway.

  • Turn on 2-step verification and set a recovery phone number.
  • Keep the password in a password manager. Never write passwords in these docs.
  • Add a second owner or admin on every platform, so access is not lost if one account is locked.
  • Later, when the domain exists, show the domain email (e.g. info@salonname.ch) on the website, in the Impressum and in the listings. Keep the Gmail only as the login. Every platform lets you change or add the contact email later, so nothing is lost.

docs.title: Google Business Profile
docs.text:
You can create the profile now and verify it later. During setup there is a "Verify later" option.

When What you can do Now (not verified) Create the profile: name, category (e.g. "Massage spa"), address, phone, website. It is not visible on Google Maps or Search yet. December, with the keys Verify the business, usually by a live video on a phone: the sign outside, the entrance, the treatment room and proof that you run the business (keys, a payment terminal). A sign with the salon name must be up before filming, a temporary one is fine. The review takes up to 5 business days. Opening date Set a future opening date (only the month and year are required, up to one year ahead). After verification the profile shows "Opening soon" up to 90 days before that date. You can publish posts and photos about the opening. Clients cannot post reviews until the salon is open. [verify] These rules come from an older Google help page.

Do not verify with another address

Do not use a home address or a "service area" to appear on Maps earlier. This breaks Google's rules, and the profile can be suspended.

docs.text:
Both apps are free and use the same encryption. For the client they look almost the same. The Business app adds tools for the salon:

Feature WhatsApp WhatsApp Business Business profile: address, hours, website, category, description, email ❌ ✅ "Business account" label for clients ❌ ✅ Catalog: services with prices and photos ❌ ✅ Greeting message for a first contact ❌ ✅ Away message: automatic reply outside opening hours, e.g. with the booking link ❌ ✅ Quick replies: saved answers, e.g. "/price", "/parking" ❌ ✅ Labels and lists: e.g. new client, booked, paid, package ❌ ✅ Link to Facebook/Instagram (WhatsApp button on the profile) and ads that open a WhatsApp chat ❌ ✅ Landline numbers ❌ ✅ (code by phone call) Path to the WhatsApp Business API (automation, Phase 2) ❌ ✅ [verify] exact migration steps

docs.title: Phone number
docs.text:
If the therapist's private number moves to WhatsApp Business:

  • her private chats (friends, family) move into the Business app;
  • her private number becomes public: on Google, the website, the Impressum, flyers and ads;
  • changing the number later means updating every listing and every printed item.

Recommendation: get a second number on an eSIM now (prepaid or a cheap plan from a Swiss provider, about CHF 0–20 per month [verify]). The phone holds both numbers: normal WhatsApp on the private number, WhatsApp Business on the salon number. It is still one phone, work and private life stay separate, and the number belongs to the salon. See meeting questions 24 and 38 in Meeting: questions before we start.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
1. Buy the domain, e.g. salonname.ch, once the name is decided.
  2. Choose an email provider. It is often the same company as the domain registrar.
  3. Create one mailbox, e.g. info@salonname.ch, and add aliases such as booking@ and hello@ that arrive in the same inbox. Aliases are usually free, so you pay for one mailbox only.
  4. Connect the email to the domain: add the MX, SPF, DKIM and DMARC records in the registrar's DNS settings (about 30 minutes; many providers do it automatically when the domain is with them). Without these records, emails can land in spam. See Domain, hosting, email.
  5. Read the email on the phone in the iPhone/Android Mail app, the provider's app or the Gmail app (add it as another account with IMAP). Google is ending the old Gmail feature that fetches mail from other accounts (POP) [verify], so use the IMAP account option.

For one therapist: Infomaniak, one mailbox, with info@ and booking@ as aliases, for about CHF 10–20 per year.

After the domain email works, change the contact email on Google Business Profile, Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, the booking tool and the Impressum. The Gmail address can stay as the login.

Booking tool emails

Neither booking tool sends client emails from our own address on the plans we tested:

  • Cal.com (free): emails come from Cal.com. With Custom Reply-To (a verified email set on the event type), client replies go to our address. Sending from our own domain needs custom SMTP, which is only on the Organizations plan.
  • Dikidi: does not send emails to clients at all. Client notifications go by Push (the DIKIDI Online app), paid SMS, WhatsApp or Telegram. Email is only used for staff alerts.

See Booking tool: buy or build?.

docs.text:
All the basic accounts are free. You pay only for ads, SMS and optional extras.

Platform Account Paid (optional) Google Business Profile ✅ Free, always Google Ads. Google never charges for the profile. Ignore phone calls that sell "Google verification" or "top ranking": this is a common scam. Facebook Page, Instagram, Meta Business Suite ✅ Free Ads; Meta Verified (a paid subscription with a badge and support), not needed WhatsApp Business app ✅ Free Meta Verified (optional). The WhatsApp Business API (Phase 2 automation) charges per message for reminder and marketing templates [verify] TikTok Business, YouTube ✅ Free Ads Apple Business Connect, Bing Places ✅ Free — local.ch / search.ch ✅ Basic listing is free Paid visibility packages (Localsearch), not needed at the start. Beware of fake "register entry" invoices, which are common in Switzerland: never pay for a directory you did not order. Booking tool Cal.com (chosen 2026-10-24): free Paid plans only for teams or extra features [verify] when needed Website Static hosting is free (e.g. GitHub Pages) or a few CHF per month — Domain + email ~CHF 10–20 per year (Infomaniak) — Second phone number (eSIM) ~CHF 0–20 per month [verify] — Payments Business bank account ~CHF 0–10 per month [verify] TWINT and card payments ~1.3–1.7% per payment; a card reader (e.g. SumUp) once ~CHF 40–80 [verify]

Minimum fixed costs before ads: about CHF 10–20 per year (domain + email), plus the second number. The real spending is advertising (see Marketing; our budget is in the private notes), and SMS reminders if we want them [verify] the price in Cal.com.

docs.title: Before opening: getting first clients
docs.text:
As soon as the name is decided:

  • Instagram and Facebook: posts like "Opening in December in Saanen", setting up the studio, introducing the therapist, what an anti-cellulite massage is. No paid ads yet; a small campaign 2–3 weeks before opening.
  • Website: a simple "Opening soon" page with the opening offer and a booking calendar that only allows dates from the opening day (in Cal.com: the date range of the event type).
  • WhatsApp Business: the business profile and an away message, e.g. "We open on 1 December, book here: link".
  • Local partners: flyers with a QR code for hotels, chalet agencies and gyms before opening.
  • Google: the profile appears after verification in December (see above).

docs.title: Ads: setup, content, placements, languages
docs.text:
Research from 2026-10-23. Ad platforms change often: check the current menus and rules in Ads Manager and Google Ads before each campaign.

This page explains how to run our ads on Meta (Instagram/Facebook) and Google. The overall plan (channels, seasons, ourselves vs. agency) is in Marketing. The technical side (tracking, consent, landing pages) is in Website: ads, SEO and analytics. Our concrete budgets are in the private notes (private/marketing-budget.md).

docs.title: Basics
docs.text:
• All ads land on our website, on the page in the ad's language (/de/, or / for English), never directly on the booking tool. See Marketing.
  • Google Search catches people who are already looking ("Massage Saanen"). It is usually the cheapest per booking for a local service: start here.
  • Meta reaches people who are not looking yet (scrolling Instagram). Good for the opening, new offers and the seasons.
  • Main number on both platforms: cost per booking, not clicks.
Google Search Meta (Instagram/Facebook) The person Searching right now Scrolling, not searching Ad Text Video, photo Strength Ready to book Awareness, opening, seasons Weakness Few searches in a small region; cannot create demand More expensive per booking; needs much content

docs.title: Ad rules for anti-cellulite (both platforms)
docs.text:
Why ads get rejected

  • ❌ No before/after images and no close-ups of "problem" skin.
  • ❌ Never address the viewer's body: "your cellulite", "do you have…". Meta's personal attributes policy forbids it.
  • ❌ No medical promises: "removes cellulite", "guaranteed results", "detox", "minus one size".
  • ❌ No nudity or sexual undertones. Show legs and back modestly, with towels. Avoid ambiguous words like "full body" or "relax completely": Google's adult content policy is strict with massage.
  • ✅ "Firming massage", "smoother, firmer-looking skin", "feel lighter", "trial session CHF …". Results vary.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Instagram is a professional account, linked to the Facebook Page and the Business Portfolio (see Account setup).
  • A payment method is added to the ad account (Business Settings → Payments).
  • The landing page exists in each language, with UTM tags, e.g. https://salonname.ch/de/?utm_source=instagram&utm_medium=paid-social&utm_campaign=opening-2026.
  • Recommended: the Meta Pixel with the booking event on the website (see Website: ads, SEO and analytics).

docs.title: How a campaign is built
docs.text:
A campaign has three levels:

Level What you set Campaign The goal (objective) Ad set Budget, schedule, audience, placements Ad The content: video/photo, text, link, button

One ad set can hold several ads, and one ad can hold several photos/videos:

Option What it is Who decides what is shown One ad = one photo or video Simplest Meta only chooses who sees it Several ads in one ad set e.g. 3–5 different videos and photos Meta gives more budget to the best one Flexible format / dynamic creative One ad with up to 10 photos/videos and several texts Meta combines them per person and placement [verify] exact names in Ads Manager Carousel Up to 10 cards in one ad that the viewer swipes The viewer

Best for us: several different ads in one ad set.

  • Since 2025, Meta's ad system (Andromeda) decides who sees an ad mainly from its content. Different videos reach different people (a local woman, a tourist looking for wellness).
  • Saanenland is a small audience. One ad repeats to the same people within 1–2 weeks (ad fatigue), and the cost per booking goes up.
  • One campaign per photo or video would split our small budget, and none would get enough data.
  • But not too many: agencies with big budgets use 10–30 ads per ad set. With a small budget, 3–5 ads is the maximum, or most of them never get shown.

docs.title: Step by step: Stories ad with a booking link (Ads Manager)
docs.text:
Go to adsmanager.facebook.com → + Create.

  1. Campaign
    • Objective: Traffic at the start. When the Pixel counts bookings, switch to Sales or Leads (optimises for bookings).
    • Special ad category: none (massage is not a special category).
    • Advantage+ campaign budget: off at the start, so you keep control.
  2. Ad set
    • Conversion location: Website.
    • Budget: a daily budget with a start and end date (e.g. 2–3 weeks before opening).
    • Location: Saanen plus 20–30 km, "People living in or recently in this location" (this also reaches tourists).
    • Age: e.g. 25–60. Keep interests broad: the region is small.
    • Languages: see Languages below.
    • Placements: Manual placements → only Instagram Stories and Instagram Reels (same 9:16 format). Audience Network off.
  3. Ad
    • Identity: the Facebook Page and the Instagram account.
    • Format: single image or video (9:16).
    • Primary text: short, e.g. "Anti-cellulite massage in Saanen. Opening in December. Book your trial session."
    • Destination: Website URL with UTM tags.
    • Call to action: Book now.
    • Check the preview for Stories → Publish. Meta reviews the ad, usually within 24 hours.

Simpler alternative: Boost in the Instagram app. Post a Story or Reel → Boost → goal "More website visits" → link and "Book now" button → audience, budget, duration. Fewer controls and less tracking, but fine for a first try.

docs.title: Where Meta shows the ads
docs.text:
Setting Who decides When to use Advantage+ placements (default) Meta: Feed, Stories, Reels, Explore, Messenger, Facebook, Audience Network Bigger budgets with ads in several formats Manual placements We tick exactly where Us: small budget, 9:16 videos made for Stories/Reels
  • Always switch off Audience Network (ads in other apps and games): cheap clicks, low quality, little control over where our brand appears.
  • In fully automatic Advantage+ campaigns, Meta may spend a small part of the budget (about 5%) on excluded placements [verify]. Not in a normal manual campaign with manual placements.
  • Brand safety: Business Settings → Brand safety → block lists of apps and sites.
  • Meta still decides which people in our audience see the ad, and when (an auction each time someone opens the app).

docs.title: Campaign types
docs.text: Type Where Content For us Search Google search results Text ✅ Start here Demand Gen YouTube (incl. Shorts), Discover, Gmail, Display Network (websites and apps), Maps (beta) Images, video, carousel Later: a small test in the opening and tourist seasons Performance Max Everywhere, Google decides Everything ❌ Not at the start: little control, needs data Display (old campaign type) Websites and apps Banners Being moved into Demand Gen (see below)

docs.title: Search campaign: best practices
docs.text:
Structure

  • One campaign with one shared budget, one ad group per language (see Languages).
  • Location: Saanen plus a radius (Gstaad, Schönried, Lauenen…).
  • Location option "Presence": people who are, or regularly are, in the area. "Presence or interest" (the default) also reaches people planning a trip to Gstaad: test it before the winter season.
  • Untick Search Partners and Display Network. Both are on by default.

Keywords

  • Local and specific: "massage saanen", "anticellulite massage gstaad", "massage gstaad".
  • Phrase and exact match at the start. Broad match only later, with Smart Bidding and conversion tracking.
  • Negative keywords from day one: erotik, erotic, thai, tantra, job, stelle, ausbildung, kurs, course, gerät, selber, gratis.

Ads (responsive search ads)

  • 2 ads per ad group. Google says a second ad gives about +6.6% conversions on average.
  • Each ad: up to 15 headlines (30 characters) and 4 descriptions (90 characters) [verify] limits in the interface. Google combines them itself.
  • Vary the headlines: place ("Massage in Saanen"), service ("Anti-cellulite massage"), offer ("Trial session CHF …"), trust ("Certified therapist"), action ("Book online today").
  • Same ad rules as above.

Assets (extensions): free and important

  • Sitelinks: Prices, Trial session, Location & parking, Vouchers.
  • Callouts: "Online booking", "Parking nearby", "DE/EN/FR".
  • Call: phone button.
  • Location: linked to the Google Business Profile (after verification).
  • Images: 1:1 1200×1200 and 1.91:1 1200×628.

Bidding

  • Start: Maximize clicks with a maximum cost per click.
  • After 15–30 tracked bookings: Maximize conversions.
  • Conversion tracking: see Website: ads, SEO and analytics.
  • Switch off automatic text customization and AI Max at the start, so Google does not write or translate ad texts by itself.
  • Check the search terms report every week.

docs.title: Demand Gen and the Display Network (ads with images)
docs.text:
These are the ads with images + text on websites, apps, YouTube, Discover and Gmail.

  • 2026 change: Google is retiring the separate Display campaign type and moving it into Demand Gen (migration tool since June 2026, complete by 2027). The Display Network stays, as a channel inside Demand Gen. "Display only" is still possible with the channel controls.
  • Formats: single image, video, carousel. Our 9:16 Instagram videos can be reused for YouTube Shorts.

Can we choose the sites or topics? Yes:

Targeting What it means Example for us Location As always Saanen + 25 km Topics Pages about a topic "Beauty & Fitness → Spas & Beauty Services", "Travel → Switzerland" Placements Specific websites, apps or YouTube channels Regional news, tourism sites, wellness channels (if they carry ads) Content keywords Pages that contain certain words "wellness Gstaad", "spa Saanenland" Custom segments People who searched for or visited certain things (10–15 search terms or URLs) People who searched "Gstaad hotel", "spa Gstaad" In-market / affinity Google's interest groups "Beauty services", "spa & wellness" Remarketing Visitors of our website who did not book "Your trial session is waiting" Lookalike People similar to our clients Later, with a client list
  • With placements, ads show only there.
  • "Optimized targeting" lets Google go beyond our audiences: switch it off for control.
  • Sites and topics to avoid are excluded mainly at account level (Content suitability).
  • Here the campaign language setting still applies (unlike Search), so separate DE and EN campaigns are possible.

Is it worth it for us? Cheap reach and good for being seen, but low intent (people read news, not looking for a massage), and few local sites carry ads. Plan: Search first. Then a small Demand Gen test (YouTube Shorts + Discover) with our existing videos in the opening and tourist seasons. Remarketing when the website has enough visitors.

docs.title: Languages
docs.text: German and English are a must; French and Italian later.

docs.title: How each platform knows the person's language
docs.text: Meta Google Search Signal The app language on Facebook/Instagram Since late September 2026: the language of the ad and the landing page, plus Google's estimate of the languages a person knows Language setting Optional language targeting in the ad set Removed for Search; still used on YouTube, Display, Discover, Gmail Result A Swiss person with the phone in English sees the English version (fine: they understand it) Google can show the English ad to a German speaker who also knows English, and the other way round

docs.title: Meta: one ad set or one per language?
docs.text:
A. Recommended at the start: one ad set with multilingual ads.

  • When creating the ad, choose a default language (German) and add languages (English, later French). Up to 48 more.
  • Each language gets its own headline and text, and can get its own image or video.
  • Meta shows each person the version in their app language; everyone else sees the default.
  • Why: the whole budget feeds one learning algorithm. In a small region, several ad sets would each get too little data.
  • Watch out [verify in Ads Manager]:
    • Text inside the video or image (subtitles, captions) is not translated: make a separate video per language.
    • One source says Reels does not serve the language versions. If so, run this ad on Stories only and make a separate ad for Reels.
    • No automatic translation: native speakers write or check every text.

B. Later: one ad set per language (language targeting German / English), each with its own budget.

  • Pros: budget control per language, clear reports.
  • Cons: the budget is split, each ad set learns separately, audiences overlap (bilingual people).
  • When: with a much bigger budget, or a different offer per audience, e.g. winter: tourists in English, spring: locals in German (anti-cellulite peak).

docs.title: Google Search: one language per ad group
docs.text:
• Per language one ad group (or campaign): keywords, ads and landing page all in German or all in English. Never mix languages in one ad.
  • Keywords in that language: DE: "massage saanen", "anticellulite massage", "massage in der nähe". EN: "massage gstaad", "cellulite massage", "spa massage near me". Some keywords are the same in both languages ("Massage Saanen"): then Google picks the ad by its language estimate, which is fine when both versions exist.
  • Landing pages: DE ad → /de/, EN ad → / (English is the default language at the main address).
  • Small budget: 1 campaign, 2 ad groups (DE, EN), one shared budget. Two campaigns only if we want a fixed budget per language (e.g. more on EN in winter).
  • AI Max and text customization off: Google confirmed that an English search can otherwise show a French ad generated by AI.

docs.title: Our setup
docs.text: Start (opening, small budget) Later (bigger budget, seasons) Meta 1 campaign → 1 ad set (Saanen + 25 km) → 3–5 ads, each multilingual (DE default + EN), a separate video per language when it has text Separate EN ad set for tourists in winter and DE ad set for locals in spring Google 1 Search campaign → ad groups DE and EN → 2 ads each, landing pages /de/ and / Separate campaigns per language; FR for the Romandie and French tourists Content Every video in 2 versions (DE and EN subtitles or voice); photos with little text Add FR, later IT

docs.title: Formats and sizes
docs.text:
Placement Format Size Files Instagram Stories / Reels (main), YouTube Shorts 9:16 vertical 1080×1920 px Video: MP4/MOV, H.264, AAC sound, 30 fps, max 4 GB. Photo: JPG/PNG Instagram/Facebook Feed 4:5 1080×1350 px Same Carousel 1:1 or 4:5 1080×1080 / 1080×1350 2–10 cards Google Demand Gen, horizontal 1.91:1 1200×628 (min. 600×314) JPG/PNG, max 5 MB Google Demand Gen, square 1:1 1200×1200 (min. 300×300) JPG/PNG, max 5 MB Google Demand Gen, vertical 4:5 960×1200 JPG/PNG, max 5 MB Google video 9:16, 1:1, 16:9 10–60 s — Logo (Google) 1:1 1200×1200 —

Meta sizes come from third-party guides: check them in the Ads Manager preview [verify].

  • Video length: 6–15 seconds works best for Stories and Reels.
  • First 2 seconds: the strongest image first (hands, oil, the therapist's face), not the logo.
  • Safe zones: keep text, logo and price in the middle. Stories: ~250 px top and ~340 px bottom free. Reels: the bottom ~35% is covered by text and buttons.
  • Sound: many people watch without sound: add subtitles burned into the video. Music: only licensed tracks, e.g. Meta's Sound Collection. Popular songs can block the ad.
  • Text on images: little, at most 5–7 words. The main message goes in the ad text.

docs.title: Quality
docs.text:
• Camera: a recent smartphone is enough. Film vertically, 1080p or 4K, 30 fps.
  • Light: daylight from a window or soft warm lamps; no hard ceiling light.
  • Stable: a phone tripod or stand. Clean lens, tidy room, no personal items in the frame.
  • Natural beats "perfect": real phone videos often work better on Stories/Reels than polished studio adverts. A professional photoshoot is great for the website; for ads, a few real phone videos are enough.
  • People on camera: written consent from everyone filmed. No client faces without permission.

docs.title: How different the ads should be
docs.text:
A different idea, not a different colour. Changing colour, font or crop gives Meta almost the same ad. Change the topic, people, setting and first seconds:

# Idea Example Why 1 Atmosphere Calm studio, warm light, oil, towels, the view of Saanen Wellness feeling 2 The therapist She talks to the camera for 10–15 s: "Hello, I'm …, this happens in your first session" Trust: often the strongest idea for a one-person studio 3 How it works 3 steps: short consultation → massage → tips for home Removes uncertainty 4 Offer "Opening in December: trial session CHF …" (photo or short video) A direct reason to book now 5 Location Saanen village, the street, the entrance, "parking nearby" Locals and tourists know where to go 6 Reviews (after opening) A real client quote, with written permission Social proof

Also vary the format: at least 1–2 videos and 1–2 photos, later a carousel.

docs.title: First content pack (before opening)
docs.text: 4 ads: therapist intro video, atmosphere video, "how it works" video, offer photo. All 9:16, with subtitles, texts in DE and EN. Start 2–3 weeks before opening. Keep 2–3 new ideas ready to swap in after 10 days.

docs.title: Running and improving
docs.text:
• Every 7–10 days: pause the weakest ad (lowest click rate, highest cost per booking) and add one new idea.
  • Refresh when frequency (how often the same person saw the ad) goes above about 3, or the cost per booking goes up.
  • Meta does not split the budget equally: one ad gets most of it. For a fair comparison of two ideas, use A/B test in Ads Manager.
  • Change one thing at a time and measure.
Metric Meaning Rough target Hook rate: 3-second views ÷ impressions Do the first seconds stop people scrolling? > 25% Link CTR: link clicks ÷ impressions Does the ad make people tap? > 1% Frequency How often the same person saw the ad < 3, then refresh Cost per booking What really matters Our limit is in the private notes

The target values are typical industry numbers, not platform rules.

docs.title: Remarketing
docs.text:
Showing ads again to people who visited our website but did not book.

  • We do not store anything about visitors. Google and Meta do: our website loads their tag (after cookie consent), they recognise the person and put them on our list. We only see the list size, never who is on it.
  • The website reports a booking to Google and Meta. The list "visitors minus bookings" is then built automatically.
  • Lists need a minimum size before ads can run (about 100 people for Meta and Google Display/YouTube, about 1,000 for Google Search [verify]). Many visitors are lost to declined cookies, Safari privacy features and ad blockers.
  • For a new local salon, remarketing becomes possible only after a few months, mostly on Meta and YouTube.
  • Technical details: Website: ads, SEO and analytics.

docs.title: Rollout
docs.text:
1. Before opening: accounts ready (Account setup), website with tracking and consent banner, first content pack.
  2. 2–3 weeks before opening: Meta opening campaign (Stories + Reels, DE + EN). Google Search campaign from the opening (or a little earlier, with the booking calendar starting on the opening day).
  3. First 4–6 weeks: weekly check of search terms, cost per booking, frequency. Swap weak ads.
  4. Opening and tourist season: small Demand Gen test (YouTube Shorts + Discover).
  5. From ~100+ people on a list: small remarketing campaign.

docs.title: Website: ads, SEO and analytics
docs.text:
Research from 2026-10-23. A technical plan for the real website, not a final decision (see the open question on the website stack).

This page explains what the website needs technically so that ads work well, the salon is found on Google, and we can measure where bookings come from. How to run the ads themselves: Ads.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
• A plain HTML/CSS/JS site is enough. Everything below runs in the visitor's browser: no server, no database, no framework.
  • One URL per language (English at /, then /de/, /fr/, /it/), with the text in the HTML.
  • Shared CSS and JS; business facts from business.yml; a check script against drift between languages.
  • Cookie banner with consent first, then the Google tag and the Meta Pixel.
  • The booking is reported from the Cal.com embed to Google and Meta: this one event drives conversion tracking, ad optimisation and remarketing.

docs.title: Structure (plain HTML, no generator)
docs.text:
We keep a plain static site, edited with an AI coding agent. The only real risk is drift: the same content exists in several languages, and one copy changes while the others do not. These rules keep it manageable:

Rule Why One page per language, like the prototype: /index.html (English), /de/index.html, … plus Impressum and privacy policy Only about 4–8 HTML files Shared files: one styles.css, one main.js (map, booking, tracking, consent) Design and logic exist only once; only the text differs per language Text in the HTML, not switched by JavaScript Google indexes each language; ads land on the right language Business facts (prices, hours, address, phone) taken from business.yml One place to change; the agent updates all language files from it Check script (e.g. make site-check): same prices and phone in every language as in business.yml, hreflang on every page, same sections in the same order Catches drift automatically Every change in all languages at once The same rule as for these docs (EN + RU)

Reconsider the approach (e.g. a static site generator) only if the site grows to many pages (blog, one page per service) or someone without AI tools must edit it regularly.

docs.title: Small additions without our own server
docs.text: Need Solution Contact WhatsApp, phone and email links; or a form service [compare] Selling vouchers online A payment link (e.g. Stripe Payment Links) or the booking tool's voucher feature Server-side tracking (optional, later) Cal.com webhook → a small serverless function (e.g. Cloudflare Workers, Netlify Functions)

docs.title: Hosting
docs.text: Option Cost Note Infomaniak (together with domain and email) A small hosting plan, a few CHF per month [verify] Data in Switzerland: simplest for the privacy policy Cloudflare Pages / Netlify Free Fast, serverless functions included; US/EU companies, name them in the privacy policy GitHub Pages Free Fine for the prototype; for the real site the options above are better

docs.title: Languages and URLs
docs.text:
• Separate URL per language: salonname.ch/ (English, the default), /de/, /fr/, /it/.
    • Ads: a German ad must land on a German page. On Google Search, the landing page language is now a matching signal (see Ads).
    • SEO: Google indexes each language separately only with its own URL.
    • Sharing: a link sent on WhatsApp opens in the right language.
    • Analytics: visits and bookings per language are visible directly.
  • <html lang="de"> (or en …) on every page.
  • hreflang tags on every page, pointing to all language versions, plus x-default.
  • / is the English page and also the x-default (for all other languages).
    • If the browser language is DE, FR or IT, a small dialog asks in that language whether to switch ("Möchten Sie diese Seite auf Deutsch sehen?"). Other browser languages see no dialog.
    • The answer is remembered, so the dialog does not come back. No automatic redirect: Google always sees the English page.
    • The cookie banner appears after the dialog is closed.
  • Language selector (a small drop-down in the header) links to the same page in the other language, not to the home page.
  • The current section is kept: while scrolling, the address follows the section (#prices, #faq …), so switching language opens the same section.
  • The prototype already uses this structure (since 2026-10-24).

docs.title: Booking calendar language (Cal.com)
docs.text:
• By default Cal.com shows the booking page in the visitor's browser language. We cannot choose it from the website.
  • Possible workaround (not decided yet, to discuss with the partners): one event type per language, each with its "Interface Language" set (event type settings; the API field is interfaceLanguage) [verify in our Cal.com account]:
Page Cal.com event type (example) Interface Language / anti-cellulite English /de/ anti-cellulite-de Deutsch /fr/ anti-cellulite-fr Français /it/ anti-cellulite-it Italiano
  • Create the English one first, then Duplicate it for the other languages and change the slug, title, description and Interface Language.
  • All belong to the same person, so they share one calendar: a booking in one blocks the time in all of them [verify] with a test booking.
  • Our own texts (service name, description, booking questions) are written in the event type's language.
  • Keep them in sync: duration, price, availability and booking questions must be the same in all four. Change one → change all.
  • The website would then give each page its own event type in data-booking-cal (from business.yml). Today all pages use one event type.
  • Cal.com is loaded only on the first click on "Book", so visitors who don't book make no request to cal.com.

docs.title: SEO basics
docs.text:
On every page

  • Unique <title> and meta description per language, with place and service: "Anti-Cellulite-Massage in Saanen | Salonname".
  • One <h1>, clear headings, the address and phone as text (not only in an image or the map).
  • Canonical URL (each language version points to itself).
  • Open Graph tags (title, description, image): the preview when the link is shared on WhatsApp, Instagram, Facebook.
  • Alt texts on images, in the page's language.

Structured data (schema.org)

  • JSON-LD block HealthAndBeautyBusiness or DaySpa, generated from business.yml: name, address, geo coordinates, phone, opening hours, prices, URL, booking link, images, sameAs (Instagram, Facebook, Google Business Profile).
  • Check with Google's Rich Results Test.

Files and tools

  • sitemap.xml with all language versions (and hreflang), robots.txt.
  • Google Search Console and Bing Webmaster Tools: submit the sitemap, watch indexing and search terms. Bing also feeds ChatGPT/Copilot answers.
  • The same name, address and phone as on Google Business Profile and all listings (see Local search presence).

Speed (also an ad factor: slow landing pages cost more per click)

  • Images in WebP/AVIF, the right size, loading="lazy" below the first screen.
  • Fonts hosted on our own server, not loaded from Google Fonts (faster, and no data goes to Google without consent).
  • Little JavaScript; load the booking widget, map and tags only when needed.
  • Check with PageSpeed Insights (Core Web Vitals) on a phone.

docs.text:
Tool Purpose Cookies / consent Google tag (Google Ads conversion tracking) Cost per booking from Google ads, remarketing Yes, after consent Meta Pixel Cost per booking from Meta ads, remarketing Yes, after consent Website statistics: GA4, or a cookie-free tool (e.g. Plausible, Matomo, Cloudflare Web Analytics) [compare] Visits, pages, languages, channels GA4: after consent. Cookie-free tools: often without a banner [verify] Google Search Console, Bing Webmaster Tools Search terms, indexing No (nothing on the website)

GA4 is free but needs consent, so it misses visitors who decline. A cookie-free tool counts all visits but does not feed Google Ads. Possible combination: a cookie-free tool for statistics plus the Google tag and Meta Pixel only for ads.

docs.title: Reporting the booking from Cal.com
docs.text:
The Cal.com window is an iframe from another domain, so our tag cannot see inside it. The embed sends JavaScript events to our page; we pass them on:

Cal.ns["anti-cellulite"]("on", {
  action: "bookingSuccessfulV2",   // [verify] event name in the Cal.com embed docs
  callback: (e) => {
    gtag("event", "booking_completed", { method: "cal.com" }); // Google
    fbq("track", "Schedule");                                  // Meta standard event
  }
});
  • People who book via the direct link (Instagram bio, Google Business Profile) never visit our website. Cal.com has its own integrations (Google Analytics, Google Tag Manager, Meta Pixel) for its booking pages [verify] which plans include them.

docs.title: UTM tags
docs.text:
Every link we place (ads, Instagram bio, Google Business Profile, QR codes, partners) gets UTM tags. The allowed values and the register of all links are on their own page: UTM links.

Example: https://salonname.ch/?utm_source=flyer&utm_medium=print&utm_campaign=opening-2026&utm_content=a6-station

Reading them needs no code: GA4, Plausible, Matomo and the ad platforms read UTM tags from the address of the first page automatically and remember the source for the whole visit. The website's job is to not lose them and to pass them on to the booking.

1. Do not lose the parameters

  • Redirects keep the query string: http → https, www → without www.
  • No UTM tags on internal links (menu, language switcher, buttons): they would start a new visit with a wrong source.
  • Canonical without parameters: <link rel="canonical" href="https://salonname.ch/de/">, so Google does not index ?utm_… copies of the page.

2. Pass the source on to the booking

The booking happens in the Cal.com iframe, so we connect booking_completed to the source ourselves:

// main.js: remember the campaign info of this visit (first page)
const p = new URLSearchParams(location.search);
const keys = ["utm_source","utm_medium","utm_campaign","utm_content","utm_term","gclid","fbclid"];
const utm = Object.fromEntries(keys.filter(k => p.get(k)).map(k => [k, p.get(k)]));
try { if (Object.keys(utm).length) sessionStorage.setItem("utm", JSON.stringify(utm)); } catch (_) {}
const saved = (() => { try { return JSON.parse(sessionStorage.getItem("utm") || "{}"); } catch (_) { return {}; } })();

// a) send the source with the booking event
Cal.ns["anti-cellulite"]("on", {
  action: "bookingSuccessfulV2",          // [verify] event name
  callback: () => gtag("event", "booking_completed", { ...saved })
});

// b) store the source with the booking in Cal.com (booking data, webhooks)
//    Cal.com accepts metadata as query parameters: metadata[key]=value  [verify]
const meta = Object.entries(saved).map(([k, v]) => `metadata[${k}]=${encodeURIComponent(v)}`).join("&");
document.querySelectorAll(".js-book").forEach(b =>
  b.dataset.calLink = `salon/anti-cellulite${meta ? "?" + meta : ""}`);
  • a) gives bookings per source in GA4/Plausible and Google Ads.
  • b) keeps the source on the booking itself in Cal.com, even when the visitor declined cookies [verify]. Useful later, e.g. "which channel brings clients who buy packages".
  • sessionStorage holds only campaign labels, no personal data, and is cleared when the tab closes. Mention it in the privacy policy [verify].

3. Analyse

Where What you see GA4 → Reports → Acquisition → Traffic acquisition Visits by source/medium/campaign; with the key event booking_completed: bookings per source GA4 → Explore Own tables, e.g. campaign × language page × bookings GA4 → Admin → Channel groups A custom channel "Print" for utm_medium=print (GA4 does not know it) Plausible / Matomo Sources with UTM filters; goals for bookings Google Ads / Meta Ads Manager Cost and bookings per campaign and ad Cal.com bookings / webhook data The source stored with each booking (point 2b), exportable to a spreadsheet

Every month: per channel, cost ÷ bookings = cost per booking, compared with the limit in the private notes.

docs.title: Remarketing: how it works
docs.text:
Visitor opens salonname.ch/de/
  → Google tag / Meta Pixel load (only after cookie consent)
  → Google/Meta recognise the person (cookie + logged-in Google/Instagram account)
  → they add the person to OUR list "website visitors"

Visitor completes a booking in the Cal.com window
  → our page catches the Cal.com booking event
  → we send "booking_completed" to Google/Meta
  → they add the person to the list "booked"

In Google Ads / Meta Ads Manager:
  audience = "website visitors (last 30 days)" MINUS "booked"
  • We never see who is on the lists, only their size.
Platform Minimum list size to run ads How long people stay on the list Google (Display / Demand Gen / YouTube) about 100 active users in the last 30 days [verify] up to 540 days Google Search about 1,000 [verify] — Meta about 100 people [verify] up to 180 days
  • Losses: declined cookies, Safari/iPhone privacy features, ad blockers. Perhaps 40–60% of visitors end up on the lists [verify].
  • Install the tags from day one: lists fill only from the moment the tag is live.
  • Later (optional): Meta Conversions API and Google enhanced conversions: the booking is also reported from a server (Cal.com webhook → serverless function), so fewer bookings are lost. Needs a privacy policy update.

docs.title: Cookie consent
docs.text:
• Advertising tags (Google tag, Meta Pixel) set advertising cookies. Google requires consent for personalised ads from users in the EEA, the UK and Switzerland [verify], and many of our clients are EU tourists.
  • Cookie banner with a real choice: "Accept" and "Decline" equally visible; categories (necessary / statistics / marketing). Open-source libraries, e.g. CookieConsent (orestbida) or Klaro [compare].
  • Google Consent Mode v2: everything starts as "denied"; tags work fully only after "Accept". The Meta Pixel loads only after consent.
  • Without consent the visitor is not tracked and not added to any list. That is normal; we lose part of the data.
  • The banner itself in all site languages.
  • The privacy policy names every tool (Google Ads, Meta Pixel, statistics tool, Cal.com, map tiles, hosting). See Website & marketing law.
  • Map: the prototype loads OpenStreetMap tiles directly. This sends the visitor's IP address to the tile server: it is mentioned in the privacy policy template; alternatively load the map only after a click [verify].

docs.title: UTM links: rules and register
docs.text:
Created 2026-10-23. Add every new link here before using it. The domain salonname.ch is a placeholder until the salon name is decided.

UTM tags are labels at the end of a link that tell our statistics where a visitor came from. They do not change the page. This page fixes the allowed values and keeps a register of every link we use, so everyone uses the same spelling and we know exactly what to search for in the reports. How the website handles them technically: Website: ads, SEO and analytics.

docs.title: How a link is built
docs.text:
https://salonname.ch/?utm_source=instagram&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=always-on&utm_content=bio
└────── page ───────┘└───────────────────────── UTM tags ─────────────────────────────────────┘
Parameter Answers Required utm_source Where from? (platform, partner, printed item) ✅ utm_medium What kind of channel? ✅ utm_campaign Which campaign or period? ✅ utm_content Which ad, button or placement exactly? Recommended utm_term Which keyword? (only for search ads, usually not needed) —

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
• Only values from the tables below. A new value is first added here, then used.
  • Lowercase, hyphens, no spaces, no accents: hotel-alpina, not Hotel Alpina or hotel_alpina. Statistics count Instagram and instagram as two different sources.
  • The language is in the page address (/de/, or / for English), not in the UTM tags. Exception: utm_content of an ad may end with the language (-de, -en) when the same ad exists in several languages.
  • Where links point: ads → the page in the ad's language (/de/, / for English), because the ad's language is known. All other links → the main address /, because the reader's language is unknown: QR codes, printed items, profile and listing links (Instagram bio, WhatsApp, Google Business Profile, Apple Maps, local.ch), the email signature. / is the English page; phones set to DE, FR or IT are offered their language in a small dialog, and the UTM tags are kept (see below).
  • Never personal data in UTM tags: no names, emails, phone numbers.
  • Never UTM tags on links inside our own website (menu, language switcher, buttons). They would start a new visit with a wrong source.
  • One link per placement: every flyer, partner and QR code gets its own link, so we can compare them.
  • Google Ads adds its own click ID (gclid) automatically. UTM tags on Google ads are optional (see Ad platform settings).
